indicators.name: Planning documents not available
indicators.description: Key planning documents are not available in the publication. These may include: procurement plans, market studies, feasibility studies among others. Check the OCDS document type codelist to see the possible documents.
indicators.tracks: Governments should provide an adequate degree of transparency across the entire cycle of the procurement process to promote fair and equitable treatment of suppliers, and to facilitate oversight. A lack of planning documents could signal poor procurement planning or integrity risks since it does not allow to verify if the planned process responds to a real need.

indicators.name: Manipulation of procurement thresholds
indicators.description: A buyer bundles tenders below the competitive threshold.
indicators.tracks: Non competitive methods increase discretion which can facilitate a corrupt buyer to award a contract to favored bidders.

indicators.limitations: Unit of analysis: Buyer. Source: Based on Compliance and strategic contract manipulation around single market regulatory thresholds – the case of Poland, Manipulation of Procurement Contracts: Evidence from the Introduction of Discretionary Thresholds, Bunching Below Thresholds to Manipulate Public Procurement

indicators.name: The submission period is too short
indicators.description: The period to submit bids is shorter than the legal threshold. The submission period starts with contracting documents being available to potential suppliers and ends with the submission deadline for expressions of interest or bids.
indicators.tracks: A short submission period leaves less time to prepare and submit bids. This makes it harder for non-connected companies to bid and to submit; well-connected firms can use their inside knowledge to win repeatedly. A corrupt buyer can give the predetermined bidder an unfair advantage by privately informing the predetermined bidder of the opportunity in advance, and by giving other bidders less time to prepare competitive bids.

indicators.name: Tender value is higher or lower than average for this item category
indicators.description: Tender value is threshold distance from mean for item category.
indicators.tracks: A larger variation in the tender value (for the same item categories) across different tenders can indicate lower value for money. Price differences for the same item across multiple contracting processes can also provide information about how competitive and efficient the procuring entity is. In addition, lower than average tender values for the same item category could indicate a procuring entity is lowering the value to avoid competitive thresholds.

indicators.name: High use of discretionary evaluation criteria
indicators.description: The proportion of contracting processes for a buyer using the non price evaluation criteria is a high outlier.
indicators.tracks: In a poorly controlled bidding process, project officials can tamper with bids after receipt to ensure that a favored contractor is selected. Non-price evaluation criteria, for instance the Most Economically Advantageous Tender criteria (MEAT), tend to be more subjective allowing issuers to favor the well-connected company, for instance: Non-price related evaluation criteria have been found to be associated with a higher probability of a single bid received (Fazekas et. al, 2016). Research in Italy found that the association between the MEAT criterion and corruption risk is stronger the more the scoring rule assigns points to qualitative (as opposed to quantitative) parameters (Decarolis, F. and Giorgiantonio, C., 2022) ⚠️However, relying exclusively on price alone can be counterproductive to achieving other procurement outcomes and strategies (e.g. sustainability goals) and non-price evaluation criteria may be recommended in specific markets. For instance, the 2014 European Directives on public procurement prescribe the MEAT criterion as the ordinary criterion for awarding public contracts and the European Commission Single Market Scorecard Indicator 6 recommends that the use of award criteria based on price alone should be less than 80%.

See OCP Red Flags Guide Annex for full methodology.

indicators.name: Wide disparity in bid prices
indicators.description: The bid price range in the same contracting process is greater than a threshold value.
indicators.tracks: A colluding bidder can mimic competition by coordinating a collusive agreement with their colluding partner to prearrange the bid prices beforehand and therefore there is no real competition. Extreme or unusual offer price distributions are found to signal collusion by academic literature Abrantes-Metz et al. (2006), Padhi and Mohapatra (2011).

indicators.name: Bid prices deviate from Benford’s Law
indicators.description: The distribution of bid prices (or tender or contract values) in a specific market deviates from Benford’s Law distribution. The indicator can also be calculated for the whole procurement dataset, however it could be less informative.
indicators.tracks: Benford’s law states that the first digit of most naturally occurring sets of numerical data follows a particular pattern, where the number 1 appears as the leading digit about 30% of the time, the number 2 as the the leading digit about 17% of the time, and so on up to 9, which should appear as a leading digit about 4% of the time. A deviation from this pattern could be a sign of price manipulation.

computation.summary: See Red flags Guide Annex for full methodology
steps: Required source concepts: Bid values Items information (to define the markets) Alternative: Tender values or contract values.
See OCP Red Flags Guide Annex for full methodology.

indicators.interpretation: Benford’s law states that the first digit of most naturally occurring sets of numerical data follows a particular pattern, where the number 1 appears as the leading digit about 30% of the time, the number 2 as the the leading digit about 17% of the time, and so on up to 9, which should appear as a leading digit about 4% of the time. A deviation from this pattern could be a sign of price manipulation.
indicators.limitations: Unit of analysis: Market. Source: Based on “Benford’s Law” in Assessing the potential for detecting collusion in Swedish public procurement, ProACT Integrity indicators and Public procurement in Brazil: Evidence of frauds using the Newcomb-Benford Law

The preferred winning bidder and project officials might also be engaged in extended negotiations over the terms of bribe demands, such as the amounts and payment schedules. Finally, project officials might deliberately delay the award beyond the bid validity period in order to support the disqualification of all bidders and the need for re-bidding (IACRC, 2012).

indicators.tracks: A short decision period can reflect a premeditated assessment, to favor a particular contractor.

computation.summary: See Red flags Guide Annex for full methodology
steps: Required source concepts: -Tender end date (or bid evaluation start date) -Award date -Procurement method.
See OCP Red Flags Guide Annex for full methodology.

indicators.interpretation: A short decision period can reflect a premeditated assessment, to favor a particular contractor.
indicators.limitations: Unit of analysis: Contracting process. Source: Based on “Length of decision period” in Uncovering High-Level Corruption: Cross-National Corruption Proxies Using Government Contracting Data

indicators.name: Decision period extremely long
indicators.description: Time interval between bid evaluation and award date is above threshold value.
indicators.tracks: A long decision period can reflect a premeditated assessment, to favor a particular contractor and signal extensive legal challenge to the tender. For instance, officials might be negotiating with the preferred bidder, attempting to create a justification to award the contract or disqualify other bids.

computation.summary: See Red flags Guide Annex for full methodology
steps: Required source concepts: -Tender end date (or bid evaluation start date) -Award date -Procurement method.
See OCP Red Flags Guide Annex for full methodology.

For instance, officials might be negotiating with the preferred bidder, attempting to create a justification to award the contract or disqualify other bids.
indicators.limitations: Unit of analysis: Contracting process. Source: Based on “Length of decision period” in Uncovering High-Level Corruption: Cross-National Corruption Proxies Using Government Contracting Data

indicators.name: Contract is not published
indicators.description: Contract document is not published.
indicators.tracks: A higher rate of awards without contract information may signal a lack of integrity. No contract can signal that the interaction between the bidders and buyer is not transparent, and relevant interested parties cannot monitor the process.

computation.summary: See Red flags Guide Annex for full methodology
steps: See OCP Red Flags Guide Annex for full methodology.

indicators.limitations: Unit of analysis: Contracting process. Source: Based on “Award contract and selection documents not all public” in Corruption in Public Procurement: Finding the Right Indicators

indicators.name: Contract has modifications
indicators.description: Contract has amendments.
indicators.tracks: Once the contract is signed, amendments or change orders can be made. While this may be legitimate in some cases, change orders can be manipulated to facilitate corruption or fraud.

indicators.name: Delivery failure
indicators.description: Supplier fail to deliver any goods, work or service on time.
indicators.tracks: Evidence shows that failure to deliver goods and services, or delivering low quality goods is a strong signal of corruption in the contracting process.

computation.summary: See Red flags Guide Annex for full methodology
steps: Required source concepts: -Contract implementation details -Contract milestones due date and delivery date.
See OCP Red Flags Guide Annex for full methodology.

indicators.interpretation: Evidence shows that failure to deliver goods and services, or delivering low quality goods is a strong signal of corruption in the contracting process.
indicators.limitations: Unit of analysis: Contracting process. Source: Based on “Failure to Meet Contract Specifications” in Guide to Combating Corruption & Fraud in Development Projects

indicators.name: Contract transactions exceed contract amount
indicators.description: Total payments to a contractor exceed the initial contract amount.
indicators.tracks: Increases in the initial contract value and/or prices of items could signal potential corruption. Cost overruns could also be a result of inefficiencies in the process or bad planning.

computation.summary: See Red flags Guide Annex for full methodology
